content.text:
I submitted **index 24 (Co 0.23 / Sb 0.77)** as the best composition. Its EQE was 0.0212%, the highest of the three measurements the budget allowed. Only 3 of the 30 library compositions were tested, so I don't know whether this is the library's best.

| Index | Composition | Why I picked it | EQE |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | Co 0.33 / Sb 0.67 | The CoSb₂O₆ trirutile phase sits here. MACE puts it on the stability hull (0 eV/atom), and it is the known Co–Sb photoanode. | 0.0056% |
| 5 | Co 0.79 / Sb 0.21 | Closest point to the Co₇Sb₂O₁₂ spinel. MACE puts it 0.03 eV/atom above the hull and MEGNet gives a 1.44 eV band gap, so it absorbs at 3.2 eV. | 0.0038% |
| 24 | Co 0.23 / Sb 0.77 | Sb-rich side, likely CoSb₂O₆ mixed with an Sb oxide (1.1 eV predicted gap). The Gaussian-process suggestion also picked this point. | **0.0212%** |

EQE rose toward the Sb-rich end, about 4× higher than the trirutile composition. Indices 25–29 have even more Sb and were never measured, so the true best may lie there.

MEGNet predicted only 0.37 eV for CoSb₂O₆, which is probably too low. I didn't rely on it. I used 1 of the 5 XRD measurements (on index 20) and never compared that pattern to reference structures. So the phase assignments above are inferred from composition, not confirmed.
